archetypes.name: The Big Six
notes: Whimsicott almost always comes and leads: Prankster Tailwind + Encore/utility enables the whole team.
Standard lead is Whimsicott + the Mega of choice (Charizard-Y or Mega Floette) for Tailwind into spread damage.
Only ONE of Charizard / Floette-Eternal comes — both carry Mega Stones and only one can Mega Evolve.
Basculegion is the endgame: Choice Scarf Last Respects snowballs after its teammates faint. Expect it in the back.
Garchomp pairs with Charizard: Earthquake is free because Charizard is airborne.
Kingambit cleans weakened boards with Sucker Punch and punishes Intimidate via Defiant.

archetypes.name: Pelipper Rain
notes: Pelipper leads to set rain; Mega Swampert doubles its Speed with Swift Swim and threatens Wave Crash OHKOs.
Basculegion is a strong co-lead: immune to Fake Out (Ghost) and KOs Incineroar with rain-boosted Wave Crash.
Archaludon's Electro Shot charges instantly in rain; Raichu leans on 100%-accurate Thunder.
Grass coverage (Grass Knot, Energy Ball) is their biggest fear — expect them to play around your Grass users.

archetypes.name: Charizard Sun
notes: Charizard-Y Drought powers Heat Wave and instant Solar Beam; Chlorophyll Venusaur doubles Speed and spams Sleep Powder.
Garchomp rides along: Earthquake is free next to airborne Charizard.
KO or pressure Charizard early — without sun the team loses most of its speed and power.

archetypes.name: Torkoal Trick Room Sun
notes: Farigiraf (Armor Tail blocks Fake Out) sets Trick Room, then Helping Hand boosts Torkoal's Eruption and Mega Mawile's Play Rough.
Under Trick Room your fast Pokemon move LAST — consider slower, bulkier picks or your own speed control.
Torkoal's Eruption is a spread nuke at full HP; chip it early or Protect through the big turns.

archetypes.name: Sinistcha Trick Room
notes: Sinistcha leads with a Trick Room setter: Rage Powder redirection guarantees the Room goes up.
Slow nukes in the back are the payoff — Conkeldurr, Mega Metagross and Kingambit outspeed everything once the Room is up.
Rage Powder redirects your single-target disruption — Dark/Ghost SPREAD damage into Sinistcha breaks the setup turn.
Kingambit fits either mode: it cleans up after Trick Room ends.

archetypes.name: Grimmsnarl Screens + Mega Staraptor
notes: Grimmsnarl leads for Prankster screens (Light Clay = 8 turns), then pivots the Mega Staraptor in safely.
Mega Staraptor is CONTRARY: Intimidate, Parting Shot, Icy Wind, Charm etc. RAISE its stats. Leave stat-droppers home.
Behind screens its Close Combat defense drops become defense BOOSTS — it only gets harder to kill.
Taunt or strong spread damage on Grimmsnarl before screens go up beats the whole plan.

archetypes.name: Sneasler Balance
notes: Sneasler leads with Fake Out pressure into Dire Claw chaos; Unburden doubles its Speed after item use.
Incineroar/Sinistcha give it pivot and redirection support; Kingambit and Basculegion clean up late.
Psychic or Ground pressure on Sneasler early stops the Dire Claw flinch/status lottery.

archetypes.name: Garchomp + Kingambit + Sylveon Goodstuff
notes: The season's most-played trio (7.1% of teams, 56.5% win rate): Garchomp spread pressure, Kingambit endgame, Pixilate Hyper Voice Sylveon.
No weather dependence — they win the neutral game with Intimidate cycling and Sucker Punch mind games.
Kingambit's Defiant punishes YOUR Intimidate; check the watch-outs before bringing stat-droppers.

archetypes.name: Mega Tyranitar Sand
notes: Mega Tyranitar sets sand on entry; Sand Rush doubles Excadrill's Speed and sand chips your non-immune Pokemon every turn.
Excadrill nearly always carries Focus Sash — its Iron Head/Earthquake/Rock Slide sweep starts once your speed control is gone.
Rotom-Wash covers their rain matchup and burns physical attackers; Aerodactyl answers sun and sets Tailwind.
Knocking out Tyranitar (or overwriting the weather) turns Excadrill back into a slow, frail attacker.

archetypes.name: Incineroar Balance
notes: Fake Out + Intimidate + Parting Shot cycle from Incineroar keeps their frail attackers safe.
Pixilate Hyper Voice Sylveon provides consistent spread damage through the pivots.
Defiant/Competitive/Contrary Pokemon on your side punish the Intimidate loop.
